newsitem.title: BELGIUM: New Year date change downs Brussels bourse.
newsitem.headline: New Year date change downs Brussels bourse.

text.p: The Brussels Stock Exchange suffered an extended seasonal hangover on Thursday as its trading system crashed due to the New Year date change.
Bourse officials could not say when trade would start.

"There is a technical problem with the change of date which is causing problems in one programme, this is currently being solved so I expect it to open in one hour," bourse director Olivier Lefebvre told Reuters at 1030 GMT.
At 1130 GMT the stock exchange was still not functioning fully.
Some traders were sceptical the bourse would open at all today as rumours circulated that the bourse did not know where the exact problem was.
"We hope the market will open before it closes again," said trader Pieter Vander Stichele at Generale Bank.
Another trader said "maybe they've put champagne in the computers".
Lefebvre said one of the problems was that orders which were placed on December 30, the last trading day of 1996, were now recognised as December 1997 orders.
This prevented investors and brokerages from changing their orders to reflect Wall Street's Tuesday plunge.
This is the most serious technical problem to have hit the bourse since a new trading system was installed last year.
